recipes.name: Mushroom Chicken Piccata
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

steps.text: Mix egg and milk together in a shallow bowl. Mix flour, salt, and paprika together in a second shallow bowl. Dip chicken into egg mixture, then lift up so excess egg drips back into the bowl. Press into flour mixture to coat both sides.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and sauté until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Add mushrooms and onion; sauté for 3 to 5 minutes.

Mix broth, wine, lemon juice, and cornstarch together in a medium bowl; pour over chicken and mushrooms. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear, about 25 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Mushroom Chicken Piccata
raw_recipe.description: The classic chicken piccata recipe, featuring chicken cooked with white wine, lemon juice, and butter, gets a lovely boost with the addition of mushrooms.

video.description: Mushrooms take classic chicken piccata to new heights of flavor.

review.reviewBody: My husband and I both thought this was excellent, plus we loved the fact that the sauce wasn't full of butter. I cooked the chicken thoroughly in the pan, removed it, then made the sauce...I didn't simmer them together as I think it would have made the breading very mushy. We can't wait to have it again! *UPDATE: As much as we liked the original recipe, we LOVE this version: Skip the whole chicken process and go straight to cooking the veggies and sauce. After sauce has thickened, toss in a green vegetable (we use broccoli florets, snap peas or asparagus), then a bunch of peeled, raw shrimp. The shrimp only need a few minutes to cook, and this will keep your green veggie from getting mushy. Serve over pasta - YUM!
Absolutely delicious! A note, if you decrease the amount of servings, do not change the amount of sauce ingredients, or will cook off all the sauce.

I'm rating this a 5-star based on modifications I made to the recipe which were based on other reviews/mods I read. I used 2 large boneless breasts, sliced long ways in 6 total pieces and flattened with a meat tenderizer. I had to increase the flour to 3/4 cup and the salt and paprika proportionately. I added olive oil to the butter, probably about 1/8-1/4 cup. Fried the chicken as instructed and then pulled the breasts out of pan and added the 'rooms and onions to pan along with 2 heaping tablespoons of minced garlic. Then placed the breasts back on top of the veggies. Covered and let it cook for 10 minutes. I didn't have any white wine and used 2 Cups of chicken broth to compensate. I also increased the lemon juice to 5-6 tablespoons and added about 4 tablespoons of rinsed capers and 4 tablespoons of chopped cilantro. Covered again and let cook for 15 minutes - removed cover for remainder of 5-10 minutes to thicken. Served over Sabzi Polo (PERSIAN rice with greens). EXCELLENT

I have made many versions of Piccata over the years and was pleasantly surprised with this one. I like the idea of combining the lemon juice, broth wine and cornstarch in a bowl first. I also like the milk and egg before the flour better than just flour. The only thing I added which was not in this recipe were capers. I have never seen Piccata without them. I sauteed 2TBS of them along with the onions, mushrooms and extra garlic removed from pan then fried the chicken. Delish!!! This is my new go to piccata. Will try it with veal sometime.

Followed recipe sections with following tweaks. Added 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp onion, 1 tsp garlic powder to flour. Cooked chicken beast completely then set aside in warmer. Sautéed mushroom & onion, then added liquid. Simmered until thickened. Tweak - added 2 tblsp lemon zest, 1 tblsp capers and simered 2-3 more minutes. Plated pasta, chicken on top and covered with Picata gravy. Amazing Flavors

I made this according to recipe and it was delicious! Lots of compliments from my daughter & son in law. I did slice my chicken breast in half lengthwise to get thinner pieces and then used a tenderizer mallet to give them uniform thickness. I browned the chicken first in butter & avocado oil, and removed it to a plate to keep warm while I sautéed the onions & mushrooms and then added the rest of the sauce ingredients. Put the chicken in the sauce for a couple minutes & served it. Delicious!

I remove the cooked chicken add chicken stock/broth to deglaze, add the mushrooms and grated garlic and a tablespoon of Organic “Better Than Bouillon” Roasted Chicken Base. This really adds flavor to the dish.

I made this dish with both boneless, skinless chicken thighs and thin-sliced chicken breasts, cooked separately in unsalted butter and kept warm in a 350° oven while I made the sauce. I only had Sauvignon blanc, so I used that, and it gave the dish amazing flavor. I reduced the sauce for about 15 minutes before putting only the chicken thighs back in the pan, because they required more cooking time. I simmered it for another 10-12 minutes before spooning the sauce over the chicken from the oven and served it all over pasta that was seasoned with butter, pink salt and pepper. My husband had three helpings, and had nothing but good things to say about this recipe. I think it's fantastic and it will be a regular dinner option in our house from now on. I'll be experimenting with serving it over rice pilaf, on a bed of cooked spinach, etc. Lots of possibilities with this fabulous dish!

I had baked chicken thighs to use somehow and choose this recipe. I sauteed a one slice of diced onions in butter, added 1 teaspoon of minced garlic and a sprinkle of paprika. I sliced the chicken off the bone, used five and added to skillet. I poured enough chardonnay in to cover the bottom of the skillet and allowed time to heat through. I sliced mushrooms and decided to add artichoke hearts to the recipe. How many you use depends on how much meat you use. This recipe is easy to adjust to the number of people eating. I added more wine for making enough gravy to coat all. When the mushrooms were tender, I thickened the sauce with a tablespoon of flour mixed into cold water, added another sprinkle of paprika and salt. When the sauce was thickened, I stirred to coat all with the gravy and sprinkled 1/3 cup fresh parsley over all. Any dish made in a wine sauce makes for a very special meal at my house.

I cubed the chicken and flattened the chicken before coating in a mix of flour, paprika, pepper and some lemon zest then pan cooking in the oil. For the sauce I used equal parts broth and wine to one-half part lemon juice, which gives it a nice lemony taste without the tartness. Also substitute artichoke hearts instead of the onion. One of my wife's favorite dishes (yes, I cook and clean up).

Came together fairly quickly for a weeknight dinner. It's a nice recipe that could easily be served for a special occasion also. I wanted a strong lemon flavor so I added zest to the sauce mixture. I cooked the chicken and moved to the oven to keep warm. Did the same with the mushrooms/onions and I added garlic, then made/reduced the sauce. Assembled on the plate...linguine, chicken, vegetables and sauce. I didn't want the breading on the chicken to get soggy and I wanted to control the amount of sauce. Very good!

This is a fabulous recipe. The flavors were well balanced. I pounded out the chicken breasts to make medallions and lessened the cooking time. I also added canned artichokes and served it over fettuccine noodles. Will definitely make this again.
The chicken was so tender. I used marsala cooking wine instead.

Not so much the recipe (which, served over some bucatini with a little whipping cream and gruyere stirred into it, had my son wolfing it down like a ravenous beast), but the website: the portion calculator, for a 1/2x serving, included 1/2 an egg(!) in the ingredients, and, when trying to print it out, it always printed out the 1x version, with 6 chicken breasts, which my son and I would probably not have made it through... I made the 1/2x version, but with the 1x quantities of mushrooms and onions and sauce, because... onions, mushrooms, and sauce! Good recipe, pretty simple to make, and great flavor.

Chicken Love This dish was easy to make and comforting to eat. The changes and additions I made were: Increased paprika to 1 teaspoon Increased lemon juice to 4 tablespoons Used Baby Bella mushrooms Added 1 T of capers Lastly, I cooked the chicken all the way through then removed it from pan to stay crispy. Then finished the rest of the recipe and poured liquid over chicken to serve and garnished with lemon wedges
Delicious and easy to make! It's a keeper.

Hi All! I tried it and felt I had to add a little more to bring out the flavor. But it was fun, and I felt the mushroom and chicken dish was fun. I will be making it again. This is the Stay-At-Home Dad signing off!
I liked the recipe but did cut chicken into medallions as the cook faster. Also Added capers and a little extra lemon and chicken stock.

I enjoyed it and so did my wife and four year old. I served it with buttered penne. The tweaks I added were adding salt and ground pepper onto the chicken breasts. I also sauteed some garlic and fresh thyme right before adding the chicken broth. I didn't have wine on hand, so I omitted it. I didn't leave the chicken in while I sauteed the onion and mushroom, as I wanted the mushrooms to lose their water entirely. I added the chicken back once I added the lemon juice and chicken broth.
This one's hard to mess up and it was really fabulous!
